prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
# Summary of the Document

This manifesto outlines a comprehensive plan for governing Britain, built around five central missions: economic growth, clean energy, public safety, opportunity, and healthcare reform.

## Economic Policy

The document emphasises fiscal responsibility through strict rules: balancing day-to-day spending with revenues and reducing debt as a share of GDP. The plan rejects unfunded commitments while promising no increases to income tax, National Insurance, or VAT for working people. Key economic initiatives include establishing a National Wealth Fund with £7.3 billion to attract private investment, creating an industrial strategy council, and reforming business rates to support high streets.

## Energy and Environment

A major focus is achieving clean power by 2030 through a publicly-owned energy company. The plan involves doubling onshore wind, tripling solar, and quadrupling offshore wind capacity. A £6.6 billion investment aims to upgrade five million homes for energy efficiency. Existing oil and gas licences will continue, but no new exploration licences will be issued. Water companies face stricter regulation regarding sewage pollution.

## Housing and Planning

The manifesto commits to building 1.5 million homes over five years through planning reform, including mandatory housing targets, prioritising brownfield development, and strategic greenbelt release. New towns will be constructed, and affordable housing supply will increase through stronger planning obligations.

## Public Services

Healthcare reform centres on reducing NHS waiting times through 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubling diagnostic scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and establishing dental rescue provisions. The plan emphasises preventative care and moving services into communities.

Education proposals include recruiting 6,500 teachers, providing free breakfast clubs in all primary schools, creating 3,000 new nurseries in primary schools, and reforming further education with specialist technical colleges.

## Criminal Justice

The document proposes neighbourhood policing guarantees with thousands of new officers, antisocial behaviour crackdowns, knife crime reduction targets (halving within a decade), and specialist units for violence against women in every police force.

## Immigration and Borders

A new Border Security Command would employ additional investigators to disrupt smuggling networks. The plan includes clearing asylum backlogs, ending hotel accommodation for asylum seekers, and creating returns enforcement units.

## Employment Rights

Proposed reforms include banning exploitative zero-hours contracts, ending fire-and-rehire practices, establishing day-one employment rights, creating a single enforcement body, and reforming minimum wage to reflect living costs.

## Devolution

Greater powers would transfer to local and regional authorities, including transport, housing, planning, and employment support. A new Council of Nations and Regions would improve collaboration between Westminster and devolved governments.

## Foreign Policy

The document affirms commitments to NATO, the nuclear deterrent, and maintaining defence spending. It proposes improved relations with the European Union through targeted agreements while remaining outside the single market and customs union. Support for Ukraine would continue, and a two-state solution for Israel-Palestine is endorsed.

## Constitutional Reform

Proposed changes include removing hereditary peers from the House of Lords, introducing mandatory retirement at 80 for peers, extending voting rights to 16-year-olds, and establishing an ethics commission. Long-term plans mention replacing the Lords with an alternative representative chamber.

## Funding

Revenue measures include extending windfall taxes on energy companies, closing tax loopholes, ending private school tax exemptions, and increasing tax compliance efforts. Efficiency savings target consultancy spending and asylum accommodation costs.
